decisions.description: The customer for the workplace grooming service is the company, which offers it as an employee benefit, rather than the individual employee
Assistants collect the pet from the employee and bring it back, so nobody has to leave work
Start with a feasibility study covering one or two companies before committing further

actions.description: Do the research for the feasibility study and produce the numbers

risks.description: Running the service needs trucks and staff to drive them, wash the dogs and walk the dogs, beyond the van already owned

open_questions.description: What the grooming products used cost

notes: The action is cited at Beth's acceptance (seg-0165) rather than at Rachel's request (seg-0162), because a request is not yet a commitment -- the frozen contract cites the earliest segment where an item is recognisable as one, and owner is whoever accepted. Applied the same way in every case with a request/acceptance pair. Two concerns raised are deliberately NOT recorded because the case resolves them: grooming eating into working hours (seg-0044) is answered by the collect-and-return decision, and parking (seg-0137) is answered by the company providing it. Recording a mitigated concern as a standing risk would reward an extractor for reading only the first half of an exchange.
